issue_context.title: single-element `.dt.time()` and `.dt.date()` should always preserve sortedness
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
In [31]: s = pl.Series([datetime(2020, 1, 1)]).dt.replace_time_zone('Europe/Amsterdam')

In [32]: s
Out[32]:
shape: (1,)
Series: '' [datetime[μs, Europe/Amsterdam]]
[
        2020-01-01 00:00:00 CET
]

In [33]: s.dt.date().flags
Out[33]: {'SORTED_ASC': False, 'SORTED_DESC': False}

In [34]: s.dt.time().flags
Out[34]: {'SORTED_ASC': False, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description


nothing major, just noticed this looking into https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/13801

### Expected behavior

Both should have an ascending sorted flag

review_comments: Technically it is sorted both Ascending and Descending at the same time 🤔 it would be some refactoring to get that done though...
@stinodego Yes I've brought up this limitation of the current sorted flag to Ritchie before. You can also run into this for larger arrays, `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]` is sorted both ascending and descending.
Why do we replace this from `compute_len` to here?

Expressions don't necessarily go down that path, e.g. the original implementation of casting `Datetime` to `Time` didn't (see https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/13812), so this just seemed simpler
